Commentary.Commentary: Well, the Aussies are up and early and have already made it to the field. Steve Smith is having a chat with his inexperienced group and gets them into a huddle. Only time will tell whether the next Starc or Cummins or Hazlewood can be picked from THIS group but irrespective, Smith has to manage with the resources he has in hand and get the best out of them. And now, a huge cheer goes across as Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill stride out to the middle, to open the innings for India. Ben Dwarshuis has the first new ball for Australia. The Indian skipper to face. Here we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

While we wait for the run chase to begin, let's take a quick peek on what's coming up on Wednesday. It is another clash between South Africa and New Zealand in another ICC event. It will be a clash between two good bowling attacks with decent batting lineups too. Both teams have been travelling to and fro from Dubai to either Lahore or Karachi or Rawalpindi, so both would be equally tired. If any, it could come down to the spin options with the Proteas preferring to stick with only Keshav Maharaj. Also, there is a bit of a cloud on Aiden Markram's fitness and should he not play, it could be a big blow to the Proteas' chances.

Australia will be slightly disappointed that they could not get to 280-290 but how can they make this look like one? Curiously, they have taken the inexperienced Tanveer Sangha to partner Adam Zampa over Spencer Johnson, which actually comes as a surprise. Johnson, much like Mitchell Johnson, has this ability to burst the ball through and a new-ball attack of Nathan Ellis and Ben Dwarshuis just does not seem to visualize any impact. So, despite this being the highest score in Dubai in this year's Champions Trophy, India will back themselves to be the first team to make it to the match scheduled for Sunday. In the last 11 ODIs played at this venue, the side batting first has successfully defended its total JUST 3 TIMES. So that makes Australia's task even tougher.

In big games, big players step up. It was Mohammad Shami in this semifinal. He was excellent with the new ball, nipping out Cooper Connolly and then came back towards the end of Powerplay 2 to get rid of Steve Smith. He eventually ended up with 3 wickets, with good support from nearly everyone, barring Hardik Pandya. The spinners squeezed the Aussies, with combined figures of 34-2-176-5. They were very accurate and forced the Kangaroos to use their feet and fair enough, some risky shots were attempted, which came off on some occasions but did not on some.

Having mentioned all of the above, Australia will be disappointed with a few things. Travis Head got to 39 but could not convert his start. Steve Smith himself got to 73 but could not convert it into a century. Towards the end, Alex Carey was stranded as he ran out of partners, as he looked good for more than 61. The Aussies were decent in their approach, mixing caution with aggression but one has to credit the Indians for being on the money consistently.

India started right on the money, not giving an inch to Australia. In fact, there was hardly any consistent run of freebies dished up by the Indians. Yes, here and there, one might have seen a loose ball and the Aussies had to make all the running. They lost Cooper Connolly early but then followed it up with 3 stands of 50-plus for the next 4 wickets. Even towards the end, Ben Dwarshuis managed to stitch a stand of 34 with Alex Carey which could prove to be crucial come the end of this game, given that Australia were 205/6 at that stage.

Hmmm... so what transpired? The moment the coin landed in Steve Smith's favour, he had no hesitation in electing to bat first. Incredibly, that's the 14th straight toss that India have lost in ODIs! But the results have not been equally corresponding. In fact, they are on a 6-match winning streak despite losing the toss and for this game, Rohit Sharma will be secretly happy that he did not have to call. On such pitches, which is fresh, it is sometimes better to lose the toss.

Let's hear what RAVINDRA JADEJA thinks about this score and the pitch as he chats with the official broadcasters. Jadeja says that the wicket looks better than the last game they played and isn't spinning as much. Reckons they need to do well in the first 10 overs and play sensibly. Adds that Steve Smith and Marnus Labuschagne bat well against spin and he had to bowl well and looked to bowl stump-to-stump. On being asked about his fielding, Ravindra has a bit of laugh and shares that he doesn't just worry about fitness and eats well too as he is 36 now and wants to enjoy things.

The highest total posted in Dubai, in this year's Champions Trophy. But is this enough? The wicket does look a lot better than the ones played previously but all the same, Australia will be happy that they have got runs on the board in a big knockout game. Just that they have a small problem. No Hazlewood. No Starc. No Cummins. No Stoinis. No Green. So because of that SMALL problem, this score is definitely competitive but by no means, matchwinning.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The on-field decision is reversed and Cooper Connolly has been relieved of his misery. The way this contest was shaping up, it was more about when rather than how. Shami was continuously teasing the outside edge and after 6 consecutive plays and misses in this over, including the wide, the 7th one brings success. It is on a length, outside off, Connolly fishes at it, again without moving his feet and this time, makes contact. But unfortunately for him, the contact is with the outside edge and the ball goes behind to the keeper, KL Rahul. There is a big noise as soon as the ball goes past the bat and India celebrate but the umpire shakes his head. The bowling side immediately takes the review, almost in disbelief, as to how could the umpire not raise his finger and UltraEdge confirms the spike when the ball goes past the bat. A torturous 9-ball duck for Cooper Connolly ends and Australia are 4/1 after 3 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: The national anthems are done and dusted and we are ready for the mega event to begin. The Indians stride out to the middle, followed by another new-look opening pair - Travis Head and Cooper Connolly. Geez, we have seen plenty of opening combinations for the Kangaroos across formats over the last 2 years, haven't we? Ever since the ever-reliable David Warner has retired, the Aussies have been trying and trying to find an effective replacement. Mohammad Shami has the first new ball in his hand and Travis Head will face. 'Play!' says umpire Richard Illingworth and off we go...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the action, but first, the officials will come out to the middle, followed by the two sets of players along with the mascots and they will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Australia first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

India's VARUN CHAKARAVARTHY is up for a quick chat. He says he is looking forward to this match. Says he is trying to process it as a normal match and trying not to get under the pressure of the occasion. Adds he is working on his release points and writing his process down, so he's not out of touch here. Says that back then, he was a different bowler who used to bowl side spin and now he bowls over spin. He made this switch in three years and playing domestic cricket in India has helped him a lot. Mentions it is a fantastic squad of four spinners. Further tells the strategy to stick on the stumps and also says it is difficult to hit the stumps. Says you need to walk into every match with a belief to win. On being asked regarding Australia having the wood over India in ICC events, Varun admits that Australia are a top side but stresses that they have done their preparations accordingly and whatever happens related to the result will happen.

The captain of India, ROHIT SHARMA, says that they were prepared to either bat or bowl and when you are in two minds, it is better to lose the toss. Adds that they have played 3 games here and each time, the surface was a bit different and you can't say much and eventually, you have to play good cricket, which will be the deciding factor. Mentions that there are 4 or 5 surfaces here and each of them are a bit different and they know it will be challenging with the slower bowlers coming into the picture and hence, they have gone with the same team.

The captain of Australia, STEVE SMITH, says it looks a pretty dry surface with dry squares and says they want to put some runs on the board. Adds they are ready to go, and the guys had a couple of good practice sessions. Reckons that it might take some turn as well. Says India are a very good side. Informs two changes - Cooper Connolly comes in for Matt Short and Tanveer Sangha comes in for Spencer Johnson.

Australia (Playing XI) - Travis Head, Cooper Connolly (In for Matt Short), Steve Smith (C), Marnus Labuschagne, Josh Inglis (WK), Alex Carey, Glenn Maxwell, Ben Dwarshuis, Nathan Ellis, Tanveer Sangha (In for Spencer Johnson) and Adam Zampa.
India (Unchanged XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel, KL Rahul (WK), Hardik Pandya, Ravindra Jadeja, Mohammad Shami, Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakaravarthy.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Australia. Steve Smith opts to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Michael Atherton and Ramiz Raja are pitchside. Atherton says it is not that hot and a gentle breeze is blowing across the ground. Also, shares the pleasing news of no chances of rain. Then informs about the dimensions and says it is 69 meters and 62 meters on the squares with 77 meters being the straight hit. He further informs that this surface hasn't been used in this Champions Trophy yet and looks pretty bare. Also observes it is dry with a few cracks here and there, but also reckons it is still battable. Ramiz joins him and says it will grip and look good for spinners. Also opines that Australia might face some challenges against the Indian spinners as their bowlers have been accurate. Thinks batting first would be a good choice.

Right then, we have generally seen on all three surfaces here in Dubai, that the pitch gets slower as the game goes on and with the threat of dew almost negligible, the team batting first could control the game well and generally, runs on the board in the big matches help that extra bit as well. Who do you reckon will come out on top in this massive encounter? We shall find out in due time. Toss and team sheets in a bit, stay tuned.

Australia have yet again shown why they are a different beast in ICC competitions, especially when it comes to the ODIs and even without their first-choice frontline pace attack, they have yet again made it to the knockout stages. They will be without Matt Short, who proved to be handy with both bat and ball, but they do have a solid replacement in the form of Cooper Connolly, who could be useful on this surface. Given it is a shoot-out game, the Aussies might not be too worried about the surface and will look just to back their strengths.

India have a tried and tested side and have a good grasp of the conditions in Dubai but they will have a bit of a selection headache. Varun Chakaravarthy outclassed the Kiwis last time around, but he played that game in place of the rested Harshit Rana, who might be back in the XI and surprisingly, we could see either Kuldeep Yadav or Mohammad Shami benched. India have made it to the Final of the ICC Champions Trophy in the previous two editions and will be looking to carry the winning momentum against the Aussies and pick up a win that might just ease the pain of that World Cup Final loss.

Time and again, we have witnessed the prowess of these two teams when it comes to this format, and they are arguably two of the best ODI sides of the last couple of decades, which makes things that more challenging and intriguing. The last time these two sides met in an ICC ODI competition was that famous World Cup Final of 2023 that Australia won on Indian soil, and they have had the upper hand in ICC ODI knockout matches in the last decade. However, India are the in-form side, and they have almost all of their first-choice players to go on and do the job for the side.

Hello and a warm welcome to cricketing fans all across the globe! The stage is set and we are just a couple of matches away from the summit clash of the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy. In the first semifinal, we have a monumental clash as two cricketing giants in the form of India and Australia lock horns at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium for a spot in the Grand Finale.
... MATCHDAY ...

The battle for supremacy in the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy is reaching its climax, with only four teams remaining. India and New Zealand have advanced from Group A, while South Africa and Australia have progressed from Group B. In the first semifinal, Group A toppers India will take on Group B’s second-placed team, Australia, at the Dubai International Stadium. India dominated the group stage, winning all three of their matches, while Australia had a disrupted campaign, with two washouts and just one completed game, which they won. Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill have both registered centuries, while Rohit Sharma has maintained his aggressive Powerplay approach but struggled to convert his starts. Shreyas Iyer has been a key performer, scoring back-to-back fifties in crucial moments, while Axar Patel has impressed with both bat and ball, controlling the middle overs and adding depth to the lineup. India’s pace attack remains a concern, with Mohammad Shami still finding his rhythm post his return from a long injury layoff. Their four-spinner strategy, highlighted by Varun Chakaravarthy’s match-winning five-wicket haul against New Zealand, has created a selection dilemma. Varun replaced Harshit Rana for that match, while Hardik Pandya took the new ball with Shami. The key question now is whether Rana returns to the XI and, if so, at whose expense. On the other hand, Australia have suffered a setback with Matthew Short ruled out due to a quad injury, with Cooper Connolly named as his replacement. Short’s absence is a blow not just to their batting but also to their bowling plans, as his off-breaks would have been valuable in the spin-friendly conditions of Dubai. The most straightforward replacement at the top is Jake Fraser-McGurk, though Aaron Hardie and Connolly offer added flexibility with both bat and ball. A positive sign for Australia is Travis Head’s return to form before rain interrupted his innings against Afghanistan. Josh Inglis and Alex Carey will also carry confidence from their heroics in the famous chase against England. As always, Marnus Labuschagne and skipper Steve Smith will be key against India’s spin-heavy attack. Despite admitting he hasn’t been at his best, Adam Zampa remains a crucial factor in conditions that should suit him. With a place in the final on the line, both teams face crucial selection decisions. Having played all their matches in Dubai, India will have a better grasp of the slow and low conditions, while Australia have spent their campaign in Pakistan, primarily in Lahore, with their Rawalpindi fixture against South Africa abandoned without a ball being bowled. A high-stakes battle awaits as two of cricket’s fiercest rivals clash in a knockout showdown. This marks their first ODI meeting since the 2023 World Cup final in Ahmedabad. Can India script a different outcome this time, or will Australia once again halt their juggernaut? Only time will tell.
